avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin/Anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Naproxen inhibits platelet function and displaces warfarin from protein binding, increasing bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, monitor INR closely and adjust anticoagulant dosing

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Aspirin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Combined NSAIDs increase gastrointestinal ulceration, bleeding, and renal toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine; use only one NSAID at a time

avoid_supplements.name: Corticosteroids
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Increased GI ulceration and bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs
avoid_supplements.action: Use lowest effective doses; consider gastroprotection with PPI if combined therapy necessary

avoid_supplements.name: ACE Inhibitors/ARBs
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce antihypertensive efficacy and increase acute kidney injury risk
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor renal function and blood pressure; consider alternative pain management

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effects may modestly increase bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for unusual bruising or bleeding; generally acceptable in moderate amounts

caution_supplements.name: Garlic
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet activity may potentiate naproxen's effects on platelet function
caution_supplements.action: Use in normal dietary amounts; monitor for bleeding signs

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have additive effects on platelet inhibition at very high doses
caution_supplements.action: Monitor at doses >3g daily; standard supplemental doses are generally safe

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (especially chronic/heavy use)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases GI irritation, ulceration risk, and hepatotoxicity; impairs platelet function
avoid_foods.action: Avoid alcohol consumption; counsel on GI bleeding risk

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce sodium excretion; excess sodium may worsen fluid retention and hypertension
caution_foods.action: Monitor sodium intake; counsel on heart failure and hypertension management

caution_foods.name: Caffeinated beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly increase GI irritation; caffeine may enhance analgesia (minor interaction)
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake if GI symptoms develop

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function, blood pressure, and signs of GI bleeding, especially in elderly patients or those with cardiovascular/renal disease. Assess for fluid retention and edema, particularly in patients on concurrent antihypertensives or with heart failure.
